body: Founder, real-time: 'build shankpit shader dynamic vbo' -- resolving the fork flagged in the earlier S144-02 recon (Apple #12388) by choosing the real GLSL/VAO/VBO path over a legacy-immediate-mode adapter. Built packages/render/gl_shader.c/.h: GL 2.0+ function pointers loaded via SDL_GL_GetProcAddress (chosen specifically for portability to the Windows mingw cross-compile target, which unlike Linux's libGL.so only gets GL 1.1 symbols for free), shader compile/link helpers with real SDL_Log error output on failure, a fixed attribute-location contract (a_pos/a_normal bound to locations 0/1 via glBindAttribLocation before linking, since GLSL 120 has no layout(location=N) qualifier) matching a dynamic VBO with the exact pos+normal vertex layout GOLDENBAND's gband_mesh_rig already emits, buffer-orphaning re-upload (same real fix GFD's battlegrounds_gui needed for its own per-frame skinned-mesh VBO). Wired a proof-of-concept into the live render loop: a small magenta square drawn through the new pipeline with an identity MVP (deliberately bypassing the legacy camera matrix stack so this proof has zero dependency on, and zero risk to, existing camera/object transform code). Live-verified under Xvfb with a real screenshot (not just a clean compile) -- the square renders correctly in the corner, and all existing fixed-function rendering (buggies, HUD, terrain, weapon UI) continues working with zero visible interference. Used a temporary auto-start-into-local-game hook to reach the render loop for the screenshot, reverted before committing -- confirmed via git diff the committed main.c has no trace of it. Native Linux build clean (gcc, no new warnings). Honest gap: the mingw Windows cross-compile target shares the same LOBBY_SRC list but couldn't be verified here (no mingw toolchain in this environment) -- portability was a design choice (SDL_GL_GetProcAddress), not yet a build-verified fact on that platform. Stage B (rewriting gband_mesh_rig's clock-advance/pose-blend internals to be tick/alpha-interpolation-aware instead of raw-dt-driven, per the earlier recon) and Stage C (wiring into SKIN_TYLER/draw_player_skin_tyler) remain open, not attempted this pass. SHANKPIT commit a5a04c2.
title: S144-02 Stage A: SHANKPIT's first real shader/VBO pipeline, live-verified
